players.product: HPC / AI data-center campuses on secured power for lease (Panther Creek PA 350 MW, Sharon PA, Moses Lake WA 18 MW, Sherbrooke QC 96 MW; RFS 2027) - converted from Bitcoin mining

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K: Moses Lake, Washington, its first HPC data center development project, is built under a turnkey agreement with Vertiv: $129 million committed for critical equipment and building materials (a $128.7 million purchase commitment payable over the next 12 months). The provider delivers engineering, project management assistance, procurement and manufacturing, site management support and factory acceptance testing for a fully integrated 18 MW hybrid-built data center designed in accordance with the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 reference architecture.
quarterly_data.figure: $129 million Vertiv turnkey commitment; 18 MW Moses Lake

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K: it is designing substantially all of its HPC data centers to support NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin GPUs, which it expects to deliver much higher energy density than Blackwell; it believes Blackwell-designed facilities may not be fully compatible with Vera Rubin's power and cooling requirements and aims to capture lease demand in 2027 for Vera Rubin-ready capacity (no assurance Vera Rubin ships on the anticipated timeline). Moses Lake is designed for NVIDIA GB300 GPUs.

Keel's 10-K power capacity as of March 27, 2026: Current Energized Capacity 341 MW, Secured Growth Capacity 430 MW, Secured Gross Data Center Capacity 648 MW, Identified Additional Gross Data Center Capacity 1,513 MW, Total Pipeline 2,161 MW (a 2.2 GW pipeline; 393 MW at December 31, 2024). By site: Panther Creek 350 MW secured (500 MW pipeline), Sharon 110 MW, Moses Lake 18 MW, Scrubgrass 1,363 MW identified (including potential on-site behind-the-meter natural gas generation), Sherbrooke 96 MW, Baie-Comeau 22 MW. It intends to allocate substantially all of this capacity to HPC data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: Total pipeline 2,161 MW; secured gross data center capacity 648 MW

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-K: fiscal 2025 revenue was $229,276 (in thousands), up 72% from $133,274: Cryptocurrency Mining $206,209, Energy sales $13,981, Electrical services $4,595, Cryptocurrency Hosting $4,491. Bitcoin Mining is its legacy business line, managed for cash generation during the redeployment of its infrastructure assets to HPC data centers; it plans no incremental capital for expanding hashrate and expects Bitcoin Mining to wind down progressively as HPC data center construction begins.
